title: Find the Longest Matching Text Window
real_world_story: A plagiarism detection system compares two documents by examining continuous sections of text and wants to determine the longest section that appears identically in both documents.

real_world_connection.system: Document similarity and plagiarism detection system
real_world_connection.input_represents: Two documents whose continuous text sections are being compared
real_world_connection.target_represents: The longest continuous matching section between the documents
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Expanding and evaluating matching windows while comparing continuous portions of both documents

problem_statement: Given two document strings, find the length of the longest continuous sequence of characters that appears in both documents. The matching sequence must consist of consecutive characters in both documents.
task: Compare continuous windows of the two documents and return the length of the longest matching window.
input_format: The first line contains the first document string. The second line contains the second document string.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the length of the longest common continuous sequence.
constraints: Documents contain only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: The longest common continuous sequence is 'cde', which has length 3.
The longest common continuous sequence is 'ello', which has length 4.

expected_algorithm.name: Sliding Window Comparison
expected_algorithm.reason: Continuous portions of the documents can be examined as matching windows, allowing the system to track the longest shared section.

hint: Consider each possible alignment between the two documents.
Maintain the length of the current continuous matching section.
Reset the current matching length when characters do not match and keep track of the maximum.
real_world_takeaway: Finding long continuous matching sections can help identify copied passages that appear directly in another document.
